$comment: U52 -- move C46, the NRST filter cap, from the reset button to the MCU end of
the reset line. Review item 15 (adversarial-ee), CONFIRMED: measured 88.97 mm
from U1.27 (R49 86.68 mm, SW6 81.54 mm). It violates the layout guide section
3 item 13 ('C46 at NRST') and ST's own recommended NRST protection, which puts
the 100 nF at the pin.
Why it matters: the H7's internal NRST filter only rejects pulses shorter than
~300 ns (datasheet VF(NRST)). Anything longer that couples into the run resets
the dash, and on a car harness that is a real event -- the same EMI argument
that made the 30 ms button debounce load-bearing.
C46 CANNOT REACH THE PIN, and that is a placement conflict rather than an
oversight. NRST is U1 pin 27, sitting between OSC_IN (25), OSC_OUT (26) and
the crystal. X1's courtyard (x 161.748..165.938) OVERLAPS U1's (right edge
162.095), so there is no channel east of pin 27 at all; the nearest free 0603
pocket is 7.20 mm and reaching it means crossing the crystal courtyard on top
or routing under it, which the guide forbids. The guide's own section 3
priority order puts the crystal and the VDDA filter ABOVE C46, so the layout
followed the ranking and C46 is what lost.
Moving X1 was considered and rejected on the numbers: X1.1 is already 2.047 mm
from OSC_IN, and any displacement that frees pin 27 makes that worse while
pushing X1 into C9/C45/C8 and dragging C41/C42 along -- degrading the guide's
highest-priority placement to serve its lowest, in the corner whose failure
mode (intermittent no-start) is the hardest on this board to diagnose.
Decision recorded 2026-08-03: leave X1 in the ideal location.
So C46 goes to the first point where /NRST leaves U1's footprint: it runs
Inner1 west along y=113.048 from the escape via, and (132.000,113.048) is the
nearest spot outside U1's courtyard that is clear on every layer. Result:
88.97 -> 35.1 mm of unshunted trace, ~2.5x less antenna and ~2.5x less series
inductance between the pin and the shunt.
R49 (10 kOhm pull-up) DELIBERATELY DOES NOT MOVE. It is a DC hold, not a
filter: at DC it pulls the whole net high wherever it sits, and the transient
path is owned by the capacitor. Moving it would buy nothing and would need a
new /+3V3 tap at the far end of the board.
NO NEW VIA IS NEEDED, which took two wrong turns to notice. Scanning the
Inner1 run for a via position clear of foreign copper on all four layers left
exactly one window, x=130.60..131.30 -- everything else is blocked by the
/BTN4 Inner1 pair. A first attempt at 132.800 cleared /BTN4 by 0.021 mm and
would have failed DRC. The second, at 130.950, passed every clearance check
and then failed on hole_to_hole: 0.258 mm against a 0.4995 minimum, from the
EXISTING /NRST via 0.508 mm away. Hole-to-hole is a drilling constraint and
applies even between two vias on the same net, which no copper-clearance
check will tell you.
That existing via at (130.442,113.048) already spans Top..Bottom, so the Top
layer is available there for free. The stub simply starts from it, and the
board gains no via at all.
C46 pad 2 is /GND and connects to the Top ground pour where it lands; the old
stub from SW6.1 to the vacated pad is deleted with it.

steps.step: 1/1  C46 100nF NRST filter: 88.97 mm -> 35.1 mm from U1.27
